newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus court stalls on Lukashenko impeachment.
newsitem.headline: Belarus court stalls on Lukashenko impeachment.

text.p: The constitutional court in Belarus on Saturday put off a decision on whether to proceed with a request from parliament to impeach President Alexander Lukashenko, the deputy president of the court told Reuters.
"We have decided to sort out how many signatures have been submitted by deputies and meet again on Tuesday," Valery Fadeyev said after leaving the court.
"There is some doubt about the case. We will have to carry out checks," he added.

Deputies had submitted more than the required 70 signatures to impeach Lukashenko but some withdrew them after Russia brokered an accord on Friday to end a political row between the president and parliament.
But Lukashenko and parliament both backed out of the deal earlier on Saturday, prompting a fresh impeachment bid. On Sunday voting ends in a national referendum on extending the president's powers.
"We cannot work out how many signatures we have. Some deputies recalled them after the deal, but others have re- submitted them," Fadeyev said.
A deputy who attended the court session said earlier that one judge was absent and the court was split 5-5 over whether to continue considering the impeachment case.
